entries.name: DefCardLessEq
entries.title: “Is not strictly larger than” binary relation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A≼B)←→(∃(f:Class)((((f class-function)∧(A⊆Dom(f)))∧(f[A]⊆B))∧(f injective)))))

entries.name: DefCardinality
entries.title: Class cardinality
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)(|K|=(On∩⋂{a|(a∈On)∧(K≼a)})))
entries.comment: Defines the von Neumann initial-ordinal cardinality |K| = On ∩ ⋂{ a : Class | (a ∈ On) ∧ (K ≼ a) }: the intersection ⋂ of the class of all ordinal sets a ∈ On into which K injects (K ≼ a), intersected with On. Because the intersection of a non-empty class of ordinals is its least element, |K| equals the least ordinal a ∈ On with K ≼ a (the initial ordinal of K) when K is a well-orderable set, and equals On ∩ ⋂∅ = On ∩ V = On when no ordinal set a ∈ On satisfies K ≼ a (i.e., when K is a proper class). Paired in the kernel with CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀A∀B((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))).

entries.name: DefCardLess
entries.title: “Is strictly smaller than” binary relation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A≺B)←→(¬(B≼A))))
entries.comment: Strict cardinality order A ≺ B ⟷ ¬(B ≼ A). Paired in the kernel with the cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))), which embodies the Global Choice / von Neumann cardinal-equipollence principle |K| ≈ K connecting 3.41 DefCardinality with 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation.

entries.name: AxmSizeLimitation
entries.title: Size limitation axiom related statement
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(X:Class)((X∈V)←→(|X|≺|V|)))
entries.comment: Von Neumann Limitation of Size in initial-ordinal form (PSizeLimAx_prf): a class X is a set (X ∈ V) iff its initial-ordinal cardinality |X| (3.41 DefCardinality) is strictly smaller than |V| = On. Combined with the kernel's cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf: (|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B), reflecting Global Choice V ≈ On), this yields (X ∈ V) ⟷ (X ≺ V) and hence Tight(V) in 3.69.

entries.name: DefHereditaryClass
entries.title: “Is hereditary” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)(Hereditary(A)←→(∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→∀(X:Class)((X⊆B)—→(X∈A))))))

entries.name: DefPowerfulClass
entries.title: “Is powerful” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(Powerful(U)←→(∀(B:Class)((B∈U)—→(𝒫(B)∈U)))))

entries.name: DefPairfulClass
entries.title: “Is pairful” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(Pairful(U)←→(∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)(((A∈U)∧(B∈U))—→({A,B}∈U)))))

entries.name: DefTightClass
entries.title: “Is tight” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(Tight(U)←→(∀(B:Class)((B⊆U)—→((B≺U)←→(B∈U))))))

entries.name: DefSingletonSet
entries.title: Singleton set
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(a:Class)({a}={x|x=a}))

entries.name: DefUnorderedPair
entries.title: Unordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(a:Class)∀(b:Class)({a,b}={x|(x=a)∨(x=b)}))
entries.comment: Defines the unordered pair class {a, b} = { x : Class | (x = a) ∨ (x = b) }. Paired in the kernel with the unordered-pair sethood axiom rule PairSetAx (PPairSetAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)(((A set) ∧ (B set)) —→ ({A, B} set))).

entries.name: DefNaturalNumberModels
entries.title: Set-theoretic models of natural numbers
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(M:Class)(NatModel(M)←→((∅∈M)∧∀(n:Class)((n∈M)—→((n∪{n})∈M)))))
entries.comment: Formal conservative definition of a set-theoretic model of natural numbers (Peano-Dedekind inductive structure under von Neumann successor): a class M is a model of natural numbers iff it contains the empty set (0) and is closed under the successor operation n ∪ {n}.

entries.name: DefClassLists
entries.title: General definition of lists of classes which applicable not only for sets, but for proper classes too
entries.formula_unicode_html: (mark(A,n) = ({{0,n}} ∪ {({{{{a}}},n}:Class) | (a ∈ A)})) ∧ (([] = ∅) ∧ (([A] = mark(A,1)) ∧ (([A,B] = (mark(A,1) ∪ mark(B,2))) ∧ (((A,B) = [A,B]) ∧ ((pr1(L) = {a | ({{{{a}}},1} ∈ L)}) ∧ (pr2(L) = {b | ({{{{b}}},2} ∈ L)}))))))
entries.judgements_unicode_html: [(A:Class), (B:Class), (L:Class), (n:Class)]
entries.comment: Defines Dunaev's tagged class lists and ordered pair (A, B) = [A, B] = mark(A, 1) ∪ mark(B, 2), where mark(A, n) = {{0, n}} ∪ { {{{{a}}}, n} | a ∈ A } tags each element a ∈ A as the unordered pair {{{a}}, n} = {{{{a}}}, n} (4 opening braces: unordered pair of the 3-fold singleton {{{a}}} and index n). Entry 3.76 DefDunaevOrderedPair expands this same definition into primitive set constructors, whereas 3.52 DefKuratowskiPair records the historical set-restricted Kuratowski pair {{a, a}, {a, b}}.

entries.name: DefKuratowskiPair
entries.title: Ordered pair(Kuratowsky's)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(a:Class)∀(b:Class)((a,b)={{a,a},{a,b}}))
entries.comment: Historical set-restricted Kuratowski ordered pair (a, b)_K = {{a, a}, {a, b}}, included for comparison with set-only theories (ZFC/NBG); in MKTD1-theory, class-level definitions (3.38, 3.76-3.78, 3.91) use Dunaev's tagged class ordered pair (3.51 DefClassLists / 3.76 DefDunaevOrderedPair), which remains sound when a or b is a proper class.

entries.name: DefBinaryUnion
entries.title: Binary union
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A∪B)={x|(x∈A)∨(x∈B)}))
entries.comment: Special Def.: (x ∪ y) = ⋃{x,y} (set-restricted); General Def.: (A ∪ B) = {z | (z ∈ A) ∨ (z ∈ B)} (general class definition).

entries.name: DefBinaryIntersection
entries.title: Binary intersection
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A∩B)={x|(x∈A)∧(x∈B)}))

entries.name: DefInductiveClass
entries.title: “Is successor-inductive (Peano-inductive)” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(X:Class)(Ind(X)←→((∅∈X)∧∀(a:Class)((a∈X)—→((a∪{a})∈X)))))
entries.comment: Successor-inductive (Peano 0-successor-inductive) in the narrowest sense: closed under 0 = ∅ and ordinal successor a |-> a ∪ {a}, as distinguished from transfinite ∈-induction (3.71 ThmTransitiveClassInduction) or cumulative 𝒫-induction (3.14 AxmRegularity).

entries.name: DefOmega
entries.title: The intersection class of all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes is called omega (⊆-minimal successor-inductive class and smallest successor-inductive ordinal)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x∈ω)←→(∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q)—→(x∈Q)))))
entries.comment: By definition, ω is not only the smallest successor-inductive ordinal, but also the ⊆-minimal (least) element among all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes in the subclass (⊆) order (Ind(ω) ∧ ∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (ω ⊆ Q)), directly expressing simple countable mathematical (Peano) induction up to ω. Conservativity & Sethood Note: because (x ∈ Q) implies (x set) by 3.02 DefIsSet whenever at least one inductive class Q exists (such as On in 3.60 or ω under 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet), the unguarded RHS ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q) is equivalent in MKTD1-theory to the strict comprehension form ((x set) ∧ ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q)); however, in a subtheory without set-existence axioms, omitting (x set) on the RHS makes ∅ ∈ ω (and hence ∅ set) derivable from DefOmega and DefInductiveClass alone. In our kernel proofs (universe_definitions.ML), ∅ set is derived explicitly from 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet (ω set), 3.07 (∅ ⊆ ω), and 3.12 AxmHeredity. Similarly, the set-restricted intersection ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} over inductive sets q agrees with the general intersection over all inductive classes Q once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet. | Special Def.: ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} (set-restricted intersection over inductive sets, equivalent to the general form once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet); General Def.: ∀(x:Class), (x ∈ ω) ⟷ (∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (x ∈ Q)).

entries.name: AxmOmegaIsSet
entries.title: “Infinity”(ω is a set)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (ω set)
entries.comment: Asserts that the ⊆-minimal successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) class ω is a set.

entries.name: ThmUniversalClassInductive
entries.title: Class of all sets is successor-inductive (Peano-inductive)
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ind(V)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_58_v_inductive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): establishes the base membership ∅ ∈ V (from 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet, 3.07 ∅ ⊆ ω, and 3.12 AxmHeredity), pairfulness V Pairful (from 3.49 DefUnorderedPair / PairSetAx), and the successor-union decomposition ∀a ∈ V, ({a, {a}} ∈ V ∧ (a ∪ {a}) = ⋃{a, {a}}) (thm_step1b_succ_eq_union_pair, which combines with unary union closure 3.86 to yield (a ∪ {a}) ∈ V).

entries.name: ThmOmegaInductive
entries.title: Intersection of all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes is a successor-inductive class itself (ω is the ⊆-least successor-inductive class)
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ind(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_59_omega_inductive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): establishes that ω itself satisfies Ind(ω), making ω the ⊆-least (minimal) element among all successor-inductive classes in the ⊆ order. (Because 3.56 DefOmega quantifies directly over all inductive classes Q without a separate (x set) guard on the RHS, Ind(ω) follows from DefOmega and DefInductiveClass alone; sethood of ∅ and ω in downstream theorems is grounded in 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet and 3.12 AxmHeredity.)

entries.name: ThmOrdinalsInductive
entries.title: Class of all ordinal numbers is successor-inductive (Peano-inductive)
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ind(On)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_60_on_inductive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved without a separate union-set axiom by showing that for any transitive set a in On, (a u {a}) c= Pow(a), so AxmExponent (PowSetAx) and AxmHeredity (HeredityAx) yield Set(a u {a}), which combines with thm_ord_succ_is_ordinal to give (a u {a}) in On.

entries.name: ThmOmegaTransitive
entries.title: ω is transitive
entries.formula_unicode_html: Tr(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_61_omega_transitive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by Peano induction on the inductive class { a : Class | (a in ω) /\ ((a c= ω) /\ (a ordinal)) } via DefOmega.

entries.name: ThmOmegaOrdinal
entries.title: ω is ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ord(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_62_omega_ordinal : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by Peano induction on { a : Class | (a in ω) /\ ((a c= ω) /\ (a ordinal)) } showing both Tr(ω) and that every element of ω is a transitive ordinal.

entries.name: ThmOmegaInOrdinals
entries.title: ω is in the class of all ordinal numbers (sets)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (ω∈On)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_63_omega_in_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): combines AxmOmegaIsSet (POmegaSetAx_prf) with Ord(ω) (thm_3_62_omega_ordinal) via DefClassOfOrdinals.

entries.name: DefIsCardinal
entries.title: “Is cardinal” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(C:Class)(Card(C)←→(∃(K:Class)(|K|=C))))
entries.comment: Conservative predicate definition (DefIsCardinal, def_is_cardinal_cert, PKernelDef_prf): a class C is a cardinal class iff C = |K| for some class K.

entries.name: ThmOmegaCardinal
entries.title: ω is cardinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_65_omega_card_sub_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): combines ω ∈ On (3.63 ThmOmegaInOrdinals) with 3.41 DefCardinality (|ω| = On ∩ ⋂{a | a ∈ On ∧ ω ≼ a} = ω by the finite-pigeonhole / initial-ordinal property of ω) and 3.64 DefIsCardinal.

entries.name: ThmOrdinalsCardinal
entries.title: On is a cardinal class
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(On)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_66_on_card_sub_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): combines Ord(On) (3.18), Burali-Forti properness Proper(On) (thm_burali_forti_on_proper: On ∉ V), and Tight(V) (v_universe_lemma_5_tight from 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation and CardLessOrderAx) with 3.41 DefCardinality and 3.64 DefIsCardinal. Since On is a proper class and every a ∈ On is a set, Tight(V) / Limitation of Size rules out On ≼ a for all a ∈ On, so {a | a ∈ On ∧ On ≼ a} = ∅, ⋂∅ = V, and |On| = On ∩ V = On.

entries.name: ThmUniversalClassNotCardinal
entries.title: Class of all sets is not a cardinal class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (¬Card(V))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_67_v_not_cardinal : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved from first principles by constructing {{emptyset}} in V, showing {{emptyset}} is not transitive and hence not in On, whereas |K| c= On for every class K.

entries.name: DefGrothendieckUniverse
entries.title: “Is a universe” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((U universe)←→(((ω∈U)∧((Tr(U)∧Hereditary(U))∧(Powerful(U)∧Tight(U))))∧Pairful(U))))

entries.name: ThmUniversalClassIsUniverse
entries.title: The class of all sets is a universe
entries.prf_constructor: v_universe_thm (PAndR_prf / POmegaSetAx_prf / PHeredityAx_prf / PPowSetAx_prf / PSizeLimAx_prf / PPairSetAx_prf)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (V universe)
entries.comment: Formal kernel proof (v_universe_thm_proof : unit -> Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check) deriving (𝘍, [] ⊢ (V universe)) from 3.68 #DefGrothendieckUniverse (PKernelDef_prf) and the 6 component lemmas: (1) (ω ∈ V) via 3.57 #AxmOmegaIsSet (POmegaSetAx_prf), 3.05 #DefUniversalClass (PKernelDef_prf), 3.08 #AxmLeftInSound (PLeftInSoundAx_prf), and 3.01 #RulClassComprehension (PComprAx_prf); (2) (V transitive) via 3.15 #DefTransitiveClass (PKernelDef_prf), 3.06 #DefSubclass (PKernelDef_prf), and 3.02 #DefIsSet (PKernelDef_prf); (3) (V Hereditary) via 3.44 #DefHereditaryClass (PKernelDef_prf) and 3.12 #AxmHeredity (PHeredityAx_prf); (4) (V Powerful) via 3.45 #DefPowerfulClass (PKernelDef_prf) and 3.13 #AxmExponent (PPowSetAx_prf); (5) (V Tight) via 3.47 #DefTightClass (PKernelDef_prf), 3.43 #AxmSizeLimitation (PSizeLimAx_prf: X ∈ V ⟷ |X| ≺ |V|), and 3.41/3.42 #DefCardinality/#DefCardLess via the kernel cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: |A| ≺ |B| ⟷ A ≺ B, reflecting Global Choice V ≈ On); (6) (V Pairful) via 3.46 #DefPairfulClass (PKernelDef_prf) and 3.49 #DefUnorderedPair sethood rule PairSetAx (PPairSetAx_prf). (An unused legacy backup constructor PVUniverseAx_prf also exists in 06_definitions.ML but is not invoked in v_universe_thm_proof.)

entries.name: AxmTarskiUniverses
entries.title: “Tarski's axiom”
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x set)—→∃(u:Class)(((u universe)∧(x∈u))∧(u set))))

entries.name: ThmTransitiveClassInduction
entries.title: General form of the transfinite ∈-induction principle on a transitive class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)∀(A:Class)((Tr(K)∧((K∩𝒫(A))⊆A))—→(K⊆A)))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_71_transitive_class_induction : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved from AxmRegularity (PEpsIndAx_prf) applied to W = { x : Class | (x in K) -> (x in A) }. Transfinite membership (∈) induction on a well-founded transitive class, contrasted with successor-induction (Peano 0-successor-induction Ind(X) in 3.55).

entries.name: AxmSoundnessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Soundness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)—→eval(𝛗)))
entries.comment: Soundness of the non-recursively-enumerable (non-r.e.) Henkin completion 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Two-Level Stratification (Why This Avoids Tarski and Löb Inconsistency): In MKTD1-system (Fact [FormulaVsSideConditionMetalevel]), object-level set/class formulas live at metalevel 0 (sort Fm = Fm₀, the object language of 𝘛 and 𝘍), whereas the reflection schemas 3.72-3.74 and the semantic evaluation functor ⟦φ⟧ (EEval) live in the +1 metalogic (metalevel 1). Because 3.72-3.74 are +1 metalevel axioms about 𝘍 rather than object-level formulas inside Fm₀, and ⟦φ⟧ is a +1 metalevel valuation functor rather than an internalized first-order truth predicate in Fm₀, the object-level diagonal lemma cannot be applied to (𝘍, [] ⊢ ·) to form a Tarski liar sentence.

entries.name: AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Semantic Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(eval(𝛗)—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Semantic completeness (omniscience, 3.73, POmnisSem_prf) of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Formulated as a separate axiom from syntactic negation-completeness (3.74 AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory, which is stated purely in terms of ⊢ and ¬ without mentioning ⟦φ⟧): neither implies the other in isolation, while under Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical model bivalence (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧) they are conditionally equivalent.

entries.name: AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Negation-Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((¬(𝘍,[]⊢‹¬𝛗›))—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Syntactic negation-completeness (3.74, POmnisNeg_prf) of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if ¬φ is not derivable in 𝘍 (¬(𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ)), then φ is derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Formulated as a separate purely syntactic axiom from semantic completeness / omniscience (3.73 AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory): in classical logic, 3.74 is equivalent to (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ∨ (𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ), and becomes equivalent to semantic completeness (3.73) when combined with Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical bivalence of M (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧).

entries.name: AxmBaseSubtheoryOfFull
entries.title: If a formula is derivable in 𝘛, then it is derivable in 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘛,Γ⊢𝛗)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Theory extension monotonicity (𝘛 ⊆ 𝘍): every theorem of the r.e. base theory 𝘛 is also a theorem of its non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍.

entries.name: DefDunaevOrderedPair
entries.title: Ordered pair(Dunaev's tagged class pair)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A,B)=(({{∅,{∅}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈A)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅}}))})∪({{∅,{∅,{∅}}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈B)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅,{∅}}}))}))))
entries.comment: Primitive-expanded form of Dunaev's tagged class ordered pair (A,B) = mark(A,1) ∪ mark(B,2) from 3.51 DefClassLists (with 0 = ∅, 1 = {∅}, 2 = {∅, {∅}} and tagged elements {{{{a}}}, n} = { {{{a}}}, n }), sound for arbitrary proper classes A, B (unlike the set-restricted Kuratowski pair in 3.52). Used as the canonical ordered pair (A, B) across class-level definitions (3.38, 3.77, 3.78, 3.91).

entries.name: ThmDunaevFirstProjection
entries.title: First projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({a|{{{{a}}},{∅}}∈(A,B)}=A))
entries.comment: Recovers A from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 1 = {∅} ({ a | {{{{a}}}, {∅}} ∈ (A, B) } = A, matching pr1 in 3.51 DefClassLists and 3.91 DefDomainRestriction) without requiring A or B to be sets.

entries.name: ThmDunaevSecondProjection
entries.title: Second projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({b|{{{{b}}},{∅,{∅}}}∈(A,B)}=B))
entries.comment: Recovers B from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 2 = {∅, {∅}} ({ b | {{{{b}}}, {∅, {∅}}} ∈ (A, B) } = B, matching pr2 in 3.51 DefClassLists) without requiring A or B to be sets.

entries.name: DefLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Nonzero limit ordinal predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)←→(Ord(A)∧((¬(A=∅))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→((B∪{B})∈A))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefLimitOrd, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): a class A is a nonzero limit ordinal (LimitOrd(A)) iff A is an ordinal, A is non-empty, and for every B in A, the von Neumann successor B u {B} also belongs to A.

entries.name: DefIndexedUnionClosed
entries.title: Indexed-union closure predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(IndexedUnionClosed(U)←→(∀(I:Class)∀(f:Class)(((I∈U)∧((f class-function)∧((I⊆Dom(f))∧(f[I]⊆U))))—→(⋃f[I]∈U)))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefIndexedUnionClosed, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): a class U is closed under indexed unions (IndexedUnionClosed(U)) iff for every index set I in U and every class-function f with I c Dom(f) and relational image f[I] c U, the union U(f[I]) belongs to U.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageLaws
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)(VStageLaws(V)←→((V(∅)=∅)∧((∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→(V((A∪{A}))=𝒫(V(A)))))∧((∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)—→(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=V(B)))})))∧∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→((A=∅)∨((∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(A=(B∪{B}))))∨LimitOrd(A)))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageLaws, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): VStageLaws(V) characterizes the transfinite recursion equations for the von Neumann cumulative hierarchy stages valOf(V, A) across base stage 0, successor ordinals A u {A}, and limit ordinals, together with the three-way ordinal classification (zero, successor, or limit). (Notational convention: here and in 3.82, 3.83, 3.88, 3.89, 3.98, the bound class variable V : Class, rendered in yellow in HTML and applied as V(A), denotes a candidate stage operator, distinguished by binding, tooltip, and arity from the 0-ary universal class constant V of 3.05 and 3.86.)

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageGraph
entries.title: Canonical von Neumann cumulative hierarchy graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (VStageGraph=⋂{V|(V class-function)∧VStageLaws(V)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageGraph, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): VStageGraph is the intersection of all class-functions V satisfying VStageLaws(V). Restricting V to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues that for each A in Dom(V) with set value V(A), there is a unique pair (A, y) in V, which by 3.25 DefValueAtArg (V(A) = U{s | (A, s) in V} = U{y} = y) forces y = V(A) and rules out non-functional multi-pair encodings. In 3.88-3.90, VStageLaws(V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis (and constructed bottom-up via 3.91-3.98 TransfiniteRec(VonNeumannStepG)).

entries.name: DefSetRankLaws
entries.title: Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(R:Class)∀(V:Class)(SetRankLaws(R,V)←→((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→Ord(R(x))))∧((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(R(x)=⋃{z|∃(y:Class)((y∈x)∧(z=(R(y)∪{R(y)})))})))∧∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(x∈V((R(x)∪{R(x)}))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankLaws, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): SetRankLaws(R, V) characterizes the set rank operator valOf(R, x) and its cumulative-stage bounding law x in valOf(V, valOf(R, x) u {valOf(R, x)}) for every set x.

entries.name: DefSetRankGraph
entries.title: Canonical Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (SetRankGraph=⋂{R|(R class-function)∧SetRankLaws(R,VStageGraph)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankGraph, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): SetRankGraph is the intersection of all class-functions R satisfying SetRankLaws(R, VStageGraph). Restricting R to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues and 3.25 DefValueAtArg (U{y} = y) that each set x in Dom(R) is paired with the unique value y = R(x). In 3.89-3.90, SetRankLaws(R, V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis on the rank operator R.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsOrdinal
entries.title: Step 0 of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of a universe is an ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((U universe)—→Ord((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step0_universe_inter_on_is_ordinal : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u : ∀(U:Class)((U universe) —→ ((∅ ∈ U) ∧ ((∅ ∈ (U ∩ On)) ∧ ¬((U ∩ On) = ∅))))): if U is a universe, then U is transitive and On is an ordinal, so their binary intersection kappa = U n On is a transitive class of ordinals and hence an ordinal.

entries.name: ThmUniverseUnionClosedFromIndexedUnion
entries.title: Step 1a of U = V_(U n On): a transitive class closed under indexed unions is closed under unary union
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)∀(f:Class)(((Tr(U)∧IndexedUnionClosed(U))∧((f class-function)∧((V⊆Dom(f))∧∀(a:Class)(f(a)=a))))—→∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step1a_union_closed_from_indexed_union : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): instantiating IndexedUnionClosed(U) with I = x in U and an identity class-function witness f on V yields f[x] = x c U and hence U(x) in U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Step 1c of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of an union-closed universe is a nonzero limit ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))—→LimitOrd((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step1c_kappa_is_limit_ord : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): for any universe U closed under unary union, kappa = U n On is an ordinal, contains 0 (via thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u from ω ∈ U and Hereditary(U)), and is closed under ordinal successor B |-> B u {B} = U({B, {B}}) by pairing and union closure; therefore LimitOrd(U n On) holds.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannStageSubUniverse
entries.title: Step 2 of U = V_(U n On): limit-stage inclusion V_(U n On) c= U from stage closure below U n On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(Tr(U)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))))—→(V((U∩On))⊆U)))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step2_v_kappa_sub_u : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the base and successor step lemmas thm_step2_v_0_in_u, thm_step2_v_succ_in_u, and thm_step2_v_limit_fam_sub_u): under VStageLaws(V), Trans(U), LimitOrd(U n On), and the stage-closure premise ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, unfolding the limit clause V(U n On) = U_{B ∈ U n On} V(B) and applying transitivity of U yields V(U n On) c= U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseSubVonNeumannStage
entries.title: Step 3 of U = V_(U n On): rank-bounded inclusion U c= V_(U n On) from stage and rank closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(R:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(SetRankLaws(R,V)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(R(x)∈U))))))—→(U⊆V((U∩On)))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step3_u_sub_v_kappa : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the inductive rank-successor step lemma thm_step3_rank_succ_in_u): under VStageLaws(V), SetRankLaws(R, V), LimitOrd(U n On), stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, every a ∈ U has R(a) ∈ (U n On), R(a) u {R(a)} ∈ (U n On) by limit closure, and a ∈ V(R(a) u {R(a)}) c= V(U n On), concluding U c= V(U n On).

entries.name: ThmUniverseEqVonNeumannStageInterOn
entries.title: Conclusion of U = V_(U n On): combining Step 1c, Step 2, and Step 3 under stage, rank, and union closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(VStageGraph)∧(SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph,VStageGraph)∧(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(VStageGraph(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(SetRankGraph(x)∈U))))))—→(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧(U=VStageGraph((U∩On))))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system synthesis theorem (thm_universe_eq_canonical_v_inter_on and thm_universe_eq_v_inter_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check across the 45 constituent lemmas in universe_definitions.ML Section 11): given VStageLaws(VStageGraph), SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph, VStageGraph), Universe(U) with unary union closure, stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, combines Step 1c (LimitOrd(U n On)), Step 2 (V_(U n On) c= U), and Step 3 (U c= V_(U n On)) via class equality antisymmetry (EqDef) to conclude LimitOrd(U n On) /\ (U = VStageGraph(U n On)).

entries.name: DefDomainRestriction
entries.title: Restriction of a class relation or function to a domain class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)(Restrict(F,A)={z|(z∈F)∧(pr1(z)∈A)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefDomainRestriction, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): Restrict(F, A) = { z : Class | (z in F) /\ (pr1(z) in A) } restricts a class relation or function F to arguments whose first Dunaev projection belongs to A.

entries.name: DefTransfiniteApproximation
entries.title: Transfinite recursion approximation predicate on ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,g)←→((g function)∧((Dom(g)∈On)∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈Dom(g))∧(X=Restrict(g,B)))—→(g(B)=G(X)))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteApproximation, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): TransfiniteApprox(G, g) holds iff g is a set-sized function whose domain Dom(g) belongs to On and for all B in Dom(g) and X = Restrict(g, B), valOf(g, B) = valOf(G, X).

entries.name: DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph
entries.title: Canonical transfinite recursion class-function graph on On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)(TransfiniteRec(G)=⋃{g|TransfiniteApprox(G,g)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g : Class | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) } is the union of the class A(G) of all set-sized transfinite approximations for generator G.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStepGenerator
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy transfinite step generator
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)(VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈Dom(f))∧(Y=𝒫(f(B))))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStepGenerator, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): VonNeumannStepG(f) = U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in Dom(f)) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(f, B))) } maps any set-sized ordinal approximation f to the union of the powersets of its values.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteApproxCoherence
entries.title: Step 1 of Transfinite Recursion on On: coherence of approximations on common ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(h:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)∧(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((∀(B:Class)∀(z:Class)(((pr1(z)∈B)∧(g(pr1(z))=h(pr1(z))))—→((z∈g)←→(z∈h))))∧(A∈(Dom(g)∩Dom(h))))))—→((Restrict(g,A)=Restrict(h,A))∧((g(A)=G(Restrict(g,A)))∧(g(A)=h(A))))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_transfinite_approx_coherence and thm_transfinite_approx_coherence_step : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_1 = { B : Class | (B in (Dom(g) n Dom(h))) -> (valOf(g, B) = valOf(h, B)) } using transitivity of the ordinal intersection Dom(g) n Dom(h) (thm_bininter_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below), concluding Restrict(g, A) = Restrict(h, A) and valOf(g, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(g, A)) = valOf(h, A) for all A in Dom(g) n Dom(h).

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionEquation
entries.title: Steps 2 and 3 of Transfinite Recursion on On: approximation sethood, union inclusion, and global recursion equation F(A) = G(Restrict(F, A)) from witnessing approximations
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)—→((g set)∧(g⊆TransfiniteRec(G))))∧(((∀(B:Class)((B∈On)—→∃(h:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((B∈Dom(h))∧((F(B)=h(B))∧(Restrict(F,B)=Restrict(h,B)))))))∧(A∈On))—→(F(A)=G(Restrict(F,A))))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_transfinite_recursion_equation, thm_approx_is_set, thm_in_approx_class_iff, thm_approx_sub_transfinite_rec, and thm_restrict_agree_from_sub : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proves (1) unconditionally that every G-approximation g is a set and a subclass of TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) }, and (2) that whenever each ordinal B in On has a witnessing approximation h in A(G) with B in Dom(h), F(B) = h(B), and Restrict(F, B) = Restrict(h, B), the global recursion equation valOf(F, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(F, A)) holds for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionUniqueness
entries.title: Step 4 of Transfinite Recursion on On: uniqueness of the transfinite recursion class-function
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(H:Class)∀(A:Class)((((∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(F,B)))—→(F(B)=G(X))))∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(H,B)))—→(H(B)=G(X))))∧((∀(B:Class)∀(z:Class)(((pr1(z)∈B)∧(F(pr1(z))=H(pr1(z))))—→((z∈F)←→(z∈H))))∧(A∈On)))—→((Restrict(F,A)=Restrict(H,A))∧(F(A)=H(A)))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness and thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness_step : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by genuine transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_4 = { B : Class | (B in On) -> (valOf(F, B) = valOf(H, B)) } using transitivity of On (thm_on_is_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below), concluding Restrict(F, A) = Restrict(H, A) and valOf(F, A) = valOf(H, A) for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannHierarchyByTransfiniteRecursion
entries.title: Application of Transfinite Recursion on On: base-stage law and unfolding of VonNeumannStepG(f) = U_(B in A) P(V_B)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)∀(V:Class)∀(A:Class)(((∀(B:Class)¬(B∈Dom(f)))—→(VonNeumannStepG(f)=∅))∧(((V(A)=VonNeumannStepG(f))∧((Dom(f)=A)∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→(f(B)=V(B)))))—→((VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})∧(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_von_neumann_hierarchy_by_recursion, thm_von_neumann_step_g_empty, thm_von_neumann_step_g_on_stage, and thm_power_cong : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proves (1) unconditionally that VonNeumannStepG(f) = ∅ whenever Dom(f) is empty, and (2) by unfolding DefVonNeumannStepGenerator and applying powerclass congruence (thm_power_cong: P = Q -> Pow(P) = Pow(Q)) that whenever Dom(f) = A, f agrees with V on A, and V(A) = VonNeumannStepG(f), both VonNeumannStepG(f) and V(A) equal U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in A) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(V, B))) }.

entries.name: DefMetaConecessitation
entries.title: CoNecessitation
entries.status: Primitive / Derived Rule (Metalevel for 𝘍, Instance Verified)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢‹𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗›)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: If a formula  is derived in 𝘍 from the empty context, then the formula 𝛗 is derived in 𝘍 from the context Γ. Why this holds for 𝘍: for an arbitrary theory 𝘞, concluding (𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗) from (𝘞, [] ⊢ ) requires 1-consistency / Σ₁-soundness of 𝘞 (and for the r.e. base theory 𝘛, asserting internal co-necessitation would by Löb's theorem 5.01 trivialize 𝘛). Because 𝘍 is a non-r.e. sound Henkin extension equipped with Soundness 3.72 ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) → ⟦ψ⟧), instantiating 3.72 at ψ :=  directly yields (𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗).

entries.name: DefReducedVarSubst
entries.title: Reduced object-level variable substitution operator SubstVar(t, x, v)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(t:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(SubstVar(t,x,v)={u|((v=x)∧(u∈t))∨((¬(v=x))∧(u∈v))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefReducedVarSubst, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): explicit 3-argument object-level substitution operator SubstVar(t, x, v) = { u : Class | (((v = x) /\ (u in t)) \/ ((~(v = x)) /\ (u in v))) } taking (1) what is being substituted (t), (2) instead of what (x), and (3) where (v), internalizing atomic variable substitution as a first-class object inside MKTD1-theory.

entries.name: ThmReducedVarSubstLaws

entries.name: DefSigmaModel
entries.title: “Dependent Sum (Sigma-Type)” model over a family
entries.prf_constructor: PKernelDef_prf (def_sigma_model_cert, [B, x, y, s, a, b])
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(B:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(y:Class)((B family)—→(((x∈Dom(B))∧(y∈B(x)))←→((x,y)∈{s|∃(a:Class)∃(b:Class)((s=(a,b))∧((a∈Dom(B))∧(b∈B(a))))}))))
entries.comment: Definitional β-membership characterization (def_sigma_model_cert, PKernelDef_prf) of the dependent sum comprehension class Σ(B) = { s : Class | ∃(a:Class)∃(b:Class)((s = (a, b)) ∧ ((a ∈ Dom(B)) ∧ (b ∈ B(a)))) } over a family B using Dunaev ordered pairs (3.76 DefDunaevOrderedPair).

entries.name: DefPiPredicateModel
entries.title: “Dependent Product (Pi-Type)” predicate and section model
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(B:Class)∀(f:Class)(((B family)∧((f family)∧((Dom(f)=Dom(B))∧∀(u:Class)((u∈Dom(B))—→(f(u)∈B(u))))))—→∀(x:Class)((x∈Dom(B))—→(f(x)∈B(x)))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_39_pi_predicate_model : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check; historical identifier DefPiPredicateModel retained for link stability): in MKTD1-theory, the dependent product predicate (f : Π(B)) is a macro abbreviation for ((f family) ∧ ((Dom(f) = Dom(B)) ∧ ∀(u:Class)((u ∈ Dom(B)) —→ (f(u) ∈ B(u))))), so the Π-elimination law ((B family ∧ f : Π(B)) —→ ∀(x:Class)((x ∈ Dom(B)) —→ (f(x) ∈ B(x)))) unfolds after macro expansion to the displayed universal projection theorem (bridged to primitive dependent product types in MKTD2-system via thm_232_pi_family_model_dependent_product_bridge).

entries.name: DefCardLessEq
entries.title: “Is not strictly larger than” binary relation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A≼B)←→(∃(f:Class)((((f class-function)∧(A⊆Dom(f)))∧(f[A]⊆B))∧(f injective)))))

entries.name: DefCardinality
entries.title: Class cardinality
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)(|K|=(On∩⋂{a|(a∈On)∧(K≼a)})))
entries.comment: Defines the von Neumann initial-ordinal cardinality |K| = On ∩ ⋂{ a : Class | (a ∈ On) ∧ (K ≼ a) }: the intersection ⋂ of the class of all ordinal sets a ∈ On into which K injects (K ≼ a), intersected with On. Because the intersection of a non-empty class of ordinals is its least element, |K| equals the least ordinal a ∈ On with K ≼ a (the initial ordinal of K) when K is a well-orderable set, and equals On ∩ ⋂∅ = On ∩ V = On when no ordinal set a ∈ On satisfies K ≼ a (i.e., when K is a proper class). Paired in the kernel with CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀A∀B((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))).

entries.name: DefCardLess
entries.title: “Is strictly smaller than” binary relation
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A≺B)←→(¬(B≼A))))
entries.comment: Strict cardinality order A ≺ B ⟷ ¬(B ≼ A). Paired in the kernel with the cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B))), which embodies the Global Choice / von Neumann cardinal-equipollence principle |K| ≈ K connecting 3.41 DefCardinality with 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation.

entries.name: AxmSizeLimitation
entries.title: Size limitation axiom related statement
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(X:Class)((X∈V)←→(|X|≺|V|)))
entries.comment: Von Neumann Limitation of Size in initial-ordinal form (PSizeLimAx_prf): a class X is a set (X ∈ V) iff its initial-ordinal cardinality |X| (3.41 DefCardinality) is strictly smaller than |V| = On. Combined with the kernel's cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf: (|A| ≺ |B|) ⟷ (A ≺ B), reflecting Global Choice V ≈ On), this yields (X ∈ V) ⟷ (X ≺ V) and hence Tight(V) in 3.69.

entries.name: DefPairfulClass

entries.name: DefTightClass

entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(Tight(U)←→(∀(B:Class)((B⊆U)—→((B≺U)←→(B∈U))))))

entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(a:Class)({a}={x|x=a}))

entries.name: DefUnorderedPair
entries.title: Unordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(a:Class)∀(b:Class)({a,b}={x|(x=a)∨(x=b)}))
entries.comment: Defines the unordered pair class {a, b} = { x : Class | (x = a) ∨ (x = b) }. Paired in the kernel with the unordered-pair sethood axiom rule PairSetAx (PPairSetAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: ∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)(((A set) ∧ (B set)) —→ ({A, B} set))).

entries.name: DefNaturalNumberModels
entries.title: Set-theoretic models of natural numbers
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(M:Class)(NatModel(M)←→((∅∈M)∧∀(n:Class)((n∈M)—→((n∪{n})∈M)))))
entries.comment: Formal conservative definition of a set-theoretic model of natural numbers (Peano-Dedekind inductive structure under von Neumann successor): a class M is a model of natural numbers iff it contains the empty set (0) and is closed under the successor operation n ∪ {n}.

entries.name: DefClassLists
entries.title: General definition of lists of classes which applicable not only for sets, but for proper classes too
entries.formula_unicode_html: (mark(A,n) = ({{0,n}} ∪ {({{{{a}}},n}:Class) | (a ∈ A)})) ∧ (([] = ∅) ∧ (([A] = mark(A,1)) ∧ (([A,B] = (mark(A,1) ∪ mark(B,2))) ∧ (((A,B) = [A,B]) ∧ ((pr1(L) = {a | ({{{{a}}},1} ∈ L)}) ∧ (pr2(L) = {b | ({{{{b}}},2} ∈ L)}))))))
entries.judgements_unicode_html: [(A:Class), (B:Class), (L:Class), (n:Class)]
entries.comment: Defines Dunaev's tagged class lists and ordered pair (A, B) = [A, B] = mark(A, 1) ∪ mark(B, 2), where mark(A, n) = {{0, n}} ∪ { {{{{a}}}, n} | a ∈ A } tags each element a ∈ A as the unordered pair {{{a}}, n} = {{{{a}}}, n} (4 opening braces: unordered pair of the 3-fold singleton {{{a}}} and index n). Entry 3.76 DefDunaevOrderedPair expands this same definition into primitive set constructors, whereas 3.52 DefKuratowskiPair records the historical set-restricted Kuratowski pair {{a, a}, {a, b}}.

entries.name: DefKuratowskiPair
entries.title: Ordered pair(Kuratowsky's)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(a:Class)∀(b:Class)((a,b)={{a,a},{a,b}}))
entries.comment: Historical set-restricted Kuratowski ordered pair (a, b)_K = {{a, a}, {a, b}}, included for comparison with set-only theories (ZFC/NBG); in MKTD1-theory, class-level definitions (3.38, 3.76-3.78, 3.91) use Dunaev's tagged class ordered pair (3.51 DefClassLists / 3.76 DefDunaevOrderedPair), which remains sound when a or b is a proper class.

entries.name: DefBinaryUnion
entries.title: Binary union
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A∪B)={x|(x∈A)∨(x∈B)}))
entries.comment: Special Def.: (x ∪ y) = ⋃{x,y} (set-restricted); General Def.: (A ∪ B) = {z | (z ∈ A) ∨ (z ∈ B)} (general class definition).

entries.name: DefBinaryIntersection
entries.title: Binary intersection
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A∩B)={x|(x∈A)∧(x∈B)}))

entries.name: DefInductiveClass
entries.title: “Is successor-inductive (Peano-inductive)” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(X:Class)(Ind(X)←→((∅∈X)∧∀(a:Class)((a∈X)—→((a∪{a})∈X)))))
entries.comment: Successor-inductive (Peano 0-successor-inductive) in the narrowest sense: closed under 0 = ∅ and ordinal successor a |-> a ∪ {a}, as distinguished from transfinite ∈-induction (3.71 ThmTransitiveClassInduction) or cumulative 𝒫-induction (3.14 AxmRegularity).

entries.name: DefOmega
entries.title: The intersection class of all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes is called omega (⊆-minimal successor-inductive class and smallest successor-inductive ordinal)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x∈ω)←→(∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q)—→(x∈Q)))))
entries.comment: By definition, ω is not only the smallest successor-inductive ordinal, but also the ⊆-minimal (least) element among all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes in the subclass (⊆) order (Ind(ω) ∧ ∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (ω ⊆ Q)), directly expressing simple countable mathematical (Peano) induction up to ω. Conservativity & Sethood Note: because (x ∈ Q) implies (x set) by 3.02 DefIsSet whenever at least one inductive class Q exists (such as On in 3.60 or ω under 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet), the unguarded RHS ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q) is equivalent in MKTD1-theory to the strict comprehension form ((x set) ∧ ∀(Q:Class)(Ind(Q) —→ x ∈ Q)); however, in a subtheory without set-existence axioms, omitting (x set) on the RHS makes ∅ ∈ ω (and hence ∅ set) derivable from DefOmega and DefInductiveClass alone. In our kernel proofs (universe_definitions.ML), ∅ set is derived explicitly from 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet (ω set), 3.07 (∅ ⊆ ω), and 3.12 AxmHeredity. Similarly, the set-restricted intersection ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} over inductive sets q agrees with the general intersection over all inductive classes Q once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet. | Special Def.: ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)} (set-restricted intersection over inductive sets, equivalent to the general form once an inductive set exists by 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet); General Def.: ∀(x:Class), (x ∈ ω) ⟷ (∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (x ∈ Q)).

entries.name: AxmOmegaIsSet
entries.title: “Infinity”(ω is a set)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (ω set)
entries.comment: Asserts that the ⊆-minimal successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) class ω is a set.

entries.name: ThmUniversalClassInductive
entries.title: Class of all sets is successor-inductive (Peano-inductive)
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ind(V)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_58_v_inductive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): establishes the base membership ∅ ∈ V (from 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet, 3.07 ∅ ⊆ ω, and 3.12 AxmHeredity), pairfulness V Pairful (from 3.49 DefUnorderedPair / PairSetAx), and the successor-union decomposition ∀a ∈ V, ({a, {a}} ∈ V ∧ (a ∪ {a}) = ⋃{a, {a}}) (thm_step1b_succ_eq_union_pair, which combines with unary union closure 3.86 to yield (a ∪ {a}) ∈ V).

entries.name: ThmOmegaInductive
entries.title: Intersection of all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes is a successor-inductive class itself (ω is the ⊆-least successor-inductive class)
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ind(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_59_omega_inductive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): establishes that ω itself satisfies Ind(ω), making ω the ⊆-least (minimal) element among all successor-inductive classes in the ⊆ order. (Because 3.56 DefOmega quantifies directly over all inductive classes Q without a separate (x set) guard on the RHS, Ind(ω) follows from DefOmega and DefInductiveClass alone; sethood of ∅ and ω in downstream theorems is grounded in 3.57 AxmOmegaIsSet and 3.12 AxmHeredity.)

entries.name: ThmOrdinalsInductive
entries.title: Class of all ordinal numbers is successor-inductive (Peano-inductive)
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ind(On)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_60_on_inductive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved without a separate union-set axiom by showing that for any transitive set a in On, (a u {a}) c= Pow(a), so AxmExponent (PowSetAx) and AxmHeredity (HeredityAx) yield Set(a u {a}), which combines with thm_ord_succ_is_ordinal to give (a u {a}) in On.

entries.name: ThmOmegaTransitive
entries.title: ω is transitive
entries.formula_unicode_html: Tr(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_61_omega_transitive : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by Peano induction on the inductive class { a : Class | (a in ω) /\ ((a c= ω) /\ (a ordinal)) } via DefOmega.

entries.name: ThmOmegaOrdinal
entries.title: ω is ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: Ord(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_62_omega_ordinal : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by Peano induction on { a : Class | (a in ω) /\ ((a c= ω) /\ (a ordinal)) } showing both Tr(ω) and that every element of ω is a transitive ordinal.

entries.name: ThmOmegaInOrdinals
entries.title: ω is in the class of all ordinal numbers (sets)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (ω∈On)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_63_omega_in_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): combines AxmOmegaIsSet (POmegaSetAx_prf) with Ord(ω) (thm_3_62_omega_ordinal) via DefClassOfOrdinals.

entries.name: DefIsCardinal
entries.title: “Is cardinal” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(C:Class)(Card(C)←→(∃(K:Class)(|K|=C))))
entries.comment: Conservative predicate definition (DefIsCardinal, def_is_cardinal_cert, PKernelDef_prf): a class C is a cardinal class iff C = |K| for some class K.

entries.name: ThmOmegaCardinal
entries.title: ω is cardinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(ω)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_65_omega_card_sub_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): combines ω ∈ On (3.63 ThmOmegaInOrdinals) with 3.41 DefCardinality (|ω| = On ∩ ⋂{a | a ∈ On ∧ ω ≼ a} = ω by the finite-pigeonhole / initial-ordinal property of ω) and 3.64 DefIsCardinal.

entries.name: ThmOrdinalsCardinal
entries.title: On is a cardinal class
entries.formula_unicode_html: Card(On)
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_66_on_card_sub_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): combines Ord(On) (3.18), Burali-Forti properness Proper(On) (thm_burali_forti_on_proper: On ∉ V), and Tight(V) (v_universe_lemma_5_tight from 3.43 AxmSizeLimitation and CardLessOrderAx) with 3.41 DefCardinality and 3.64 DefIsCardinal. Since On is a proper class and every a ∈ On is a set, Tight(V) / Limitation of Size rules out On ≼ a for all a ∈ On, so {a | a ∈ On ∧ On ≼ a} = ∅, ⋂∅ = V, and |On| = On ∩ V = On.

entries.name: ThmUniversalClassNotCardinal
entries.title: Class of all sets is not a cardinal class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (¬Card(V))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_67_v_not_cardinal : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved from first principles by constructing {{emptyset}} in V, showing {{emptyset}} is not transitive and hence not in On, whereas |K| c= On for every class K.

entries.name: DefGrothendieckUniverse
entries.title: “Is a universe” predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((U universe)←→(((ω∈U)∧((Tr(U)∧Hereditary(U))∧(Powerful(U)∧Tight(U))))∧Pairful(U))))

entries.name: ThmUniversalClassIsUniverse
entries.title: The class of all sets is a universe
entries.prf_constructor: v_universe_thm (PAndR_prf / POmegaSetAx_prf / PHeredityAx_prf / PPowSetAx_prf / PSizeLimAx_prf / PPairSetAx_prf)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (V universe)
entries.comment: Formal kernel proof (v_universe_thm_proof : unit -> Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check) deriving (𝘍, [] ⊢ (V universe)) from 3.68 #DefGrothendieckUniverse (PKernelDef_prf) and the 6 component lemmas: (1) (ω ∈ V) via 3.57 #AxmOmegaIsSet (POmegaSetAx_prf), 3.05 #DefUniversalClass (PKernelDef_prf), 3.08 #AxmLeftInSound (PLeftInSoundAx_prf), and 3.01 #RulClassComprehension (PComprAx_prf); (2) (V transitive) via 3.15 #DefTransitiveClass (PKernelDef_prf), 3.06 #DefSubclass (PKernelDef_prf), and 3.02 #DefIsSet (PKernelDef_prf); (3) (V Hereditary) via 3.44 #DefHereditaryClass (PKernelDef_prf) and 3.12 #AxmHeredity (PHeredityAx_prf); (4) (V Powerful) via 3.45 #DefPowerfulClass (PKernelDef_prf) and 3.13 #AxmExponent (PPowSetAx_prf); (5) (V Tight) via 3.47 #DefTightClass (PKernelDef_prf), 3.43 #AxmSizeLimitation (PSizeLimAx_prf: X ∈ V ⟷ |X| ≺ |V|), and 3.41/3.42 #DefCardinality/#DefCardLess via the kernel cardinal-order reflection rule CardLessOrderAx (PCardLessOrderAx_prf in 06_definitions.ML: |A| ≺ |B| ⟷ A ≺ B, reflecting Global Choice V ≈ On); (6) (V Pairful) via 3.46 #DefPairfulClass (PKernelDef_prf) and 3.49 #DefUnorderedPair sethood rule PairSetAx (PPairSetAx_prf). (An unused legacy backup constructor PVUniverseAx_prf also exists in 06_definitions.ML but is not invoked in v_universe_thm_proof.)

entries.name: AxmTarskiUniverses
entries.title: “Tarski's axiom”
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(x:Class)((x set)—→∃(u:Class)(((u universe)∧(x∈u))∧(u set))))

entries.name: ThmTransitiveClassInduction
entries.title: General form of the transfinite ∈-induction principle on a transitive class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(K:Class)∀(A:Class)((Tr(K)∧((K∩𝒫(A))⊆A))—→(K⊆A)))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_3_71_transitive_class_induction : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved from AxmRegularity (PEpsIndAx_prf) applied to W = { x : Class | (x in K) -> (x in A) }. Transfinite membership (∈) induction on a well-founded transitive class, contrasted with successor-induction (Peano 0-successor-induction Ind(X) in 3.55).

entries.name: AxmSoundnessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Soundness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)—→eval(𝛗)))
entries.comment: Soundness of the non-recursively-enumerable (non-r.e.) Henkin completion 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Two-Level Stratification (Why This Avoids Tarski and Löb Inconsistency): In MKTD1-system (Fact [FormulaVsSideConditionMetalevel]), object-level set/class formulas live at metalevel 0 (sort Fm = Fm₀, the object language of 𝘛 and 𝘍), whereas the reflection schemas 3.72-3.74 and the semantic evaluation functor ⟦φ⟧ (EEval) live in the +1 metalogic (metalevel 1). Because 3.72-3.74 are +1 metalevel axioms about 𝘍 rather than object-level formulas inside Fm₀, and ⟦φ⟧ is a +1 metalevel valuation functor rather than an internalized first-order truth predicate in Fm₀, the object-level diagonal lemma cannot be applied to (𝘍, [] ⊢ ·) to form a Tarski liar sentence.

entries.name: AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Semantic Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)(eval(𝛗)—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Semantic completeness (omniscience, 3.73, POmnisSem_prf) of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Formulated as a separate axiom from syntactic negation-completeness (3.74 AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory, which is stated purely in terms of ⊢ and ¬ without mentioning ⟦φ⟧): neither implies the other in isolation, while under Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical model bivalence (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧) they are conditionally equivalent.

entries.name: AxmNegationCompletenessOfFullTheory
entries.title: Negation-Completeness of the theory 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(𝛗:Fm)((¬(𝘍,[]⊢‹¬𝛗›))—→(𝘍,[]⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Syntactic negation-completeness (3.74, POmnisNeg_prf) of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍 at metalevel 1: for every object-level sentence φ : Fm, if ¬φ is not derivable in 𝘍 (¬(𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ)), then φ is derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Formulated as a separate purely syntactic axiom from semantic completeness / omniscience (3.73 AxmSemanticCompletenessOfFullTheory): in classical logic, 3.74 is equivalent to (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ∨ (𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ), and becomes equivalent to semantic completeness (3.73) when combined with Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72) and classical bivalence of M (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧).

entries.name: AxmBaseSubtheoryOfFull
entries.title: If a formula is derivable in 𝘛, then it is derivable in 𝘍
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘛,Γ⊢𝛗)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: Theory extension monotonicity (𝘛 ⊆ 𝘍): every theorem of the r.e. base theory 𝘛 is also a theorem of its non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍.

entries.name: DefDunaevOrderedPair
entries.title: Ordered pair(Dunaev's tagged class pair)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)((A,B)=(({{∅,{∅}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈A)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅}}))})∪({{∅,{∅,{∅}}}}∪{x|∃(a:Class)((a∈B)∧(x={{{{a}}},{∅,{∅}}}))}))))
entries.comment: Primitive-expanded form of Dunaev's tagged class ordered pair (A,B) = mark(A,1) ∪ mark(B,2) from 3.51 DefClassLists (with 0 = ∅, 1 = {∅}, 2 = {∅, {∅}} and tagged elements {{{{a}}}, n} = { {{{a}}}, n }), sound for arbitrary proper classes A, B (unlike the set-restricted Kuratowski pair in 3.52). Used as the canonical ordered pair (A, B) across class-level definitions (3.38, 3.77, 3.78, 3.91).

entries.name: ThmDunaevFirstProjection
entries.title: First projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({a|{{{{a}}},{∅}}∈(A,B)}=A))
entries.comment: Recovers A from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 1 = {∅} ({ a | {{{{a}}}, {∅}} ∈ (A, B) } = A, matching pr1 in 3.51 DefClassLists and 3.91 DefDomainRestriction) without requiring A or B to be sets.

entries.name: ThmDunaevSecondProjection
entries.title: Second projection of Dunaev's tagged ordered pair
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)∀(B:Class)({b|{{{{b}}},{∅,{∅}}}∈(A,B)}=B))
entries.comment: Recovers B from Dunaev's tagged ordered pair (A, B) via tag 2 = {∅, {∅}} ({ b | {{{{b}}}, {∅, {∅}}} ∈ (A, B) } = B, matching pr2 in 3.51 DefClassLists) without requiring A or B to be sets.

entries.name: DefLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Nonzero limit ordinal predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)←→(Ord(A)∧((¬(A=∅))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→((B∪{B})∈A))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefLimitOrd, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): a class A is a nonzero limit ordinal (LimitOrd(A)) iff A is an ordinal, A is non-empty, and for every B in A, the von Neumann successor B u {B} also belongs to A.

entries.name: DefIndexedUnionClosed
entries.title: Indexed-union closure predicate
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(IndexedUnionClosed(U)←→(∀(I:Class)∀(f:Class)(((I∈U)∧((f class-function)∧((I⊆Dom(f))∧(f[I]⊆U))))—→(⋃f[I]∈U)))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefIndexedUnionClosed, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): a class U is closed under indexed unions (IndexedUnionClosed(U)) iff for every index set I in U and every class-function f with I c Dom(f) and relational image f[I] c U, the union U(f[I]) belongs to U.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageLaws
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)(VStageLaws(V)←→((V(∅)=∅)∧((∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→(V((A∪{A}))=𝒫(V(A)))))∧((∀(A:Class)(LimitOrd(A)—→(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=V(B)))})))∧∀(A:Class)(Ord(A)—→((A=∅)∨((∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(A=(B∪{B}))))∨LimitOrd(A)))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageLaws, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): VStageLaws(V) characterizes the transfinite recursion equations for the von Neumann cumulative hierarchy stages valOf(V, A) across base stage 0, successor ordinals A u {A}, and limit ordinals, together with the three-way ordinal classification (zero, successor, or limit). (Notational convention: here and in 3.82, 3.83, 3.88, 3.89, 3.98, the bound class variable V : Class, rendered in yellow in HTML and applied as V(A), denotes a candidate stage operator, distinguished by binding, tooltip, and arity from the 0-ary universal class constant V of 3.05 and 3.86.)

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStageGraph
entries.title: Canonical von Neumann cumulative hierarchy graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (VStageGraph=⋂{V|(V class-function)∧VStageLaws(V)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStageGraph, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): VStageGraph is the intersection of all class-functions V satisfying VStageLaws(V). Restricting V to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues that for each A in Dom(V) with set value V(A), there is a unique pair (A, y) in V, which by 3.25 DefValueAtArg (V(A) = U{s | (A, s) in V} = U{y} = y) forces y = V(A) and rules out non-functional multi-pair encodings. In 3.88-3.90, VStageLaws(V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis (and constructed bottom-up via 3.91-3.98 TransfiniteRec(VonNeumannStepG)).

entries.name: DefSetRankLaws
entries.title: Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank recursion laws
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(R:Class)∀(V:Class)(SetRankLaws(R,V)←→((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→Ord(R(x))))∧((∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(R(x)=⋃{z|∃(y:Class)((y∈x)∧(z=(R(y)∪{R(y)})))})))∧∀(x:Class)((x set)—→(x∈V((R(x)∪{R(x)}))))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankLaws, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): SetRankLaws(R, V) characterizes the set rank operator valOf(R, x) and its cumulative-stage bounding law x in valOf(V, valOf(R, x) u {valOf(R, x)}) for every set x.

entries.name: DefSetRankGraph
entries.title: Canonical Mirimanoff-von Neumann set rank graph
entries.formula_unicode_html: (SetRankGraph=⋂{R|(R class-function)∧SetRankLaws(R,VStageGraph)})
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefSetRankGraph, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): SetRankGraph is the intersection of all class-functions R satisfying SetRankLaws(R, VStageGraph). Restricting R to class-functions (3.32 DefClassFunction) ensures via 3.29 DefHasConcentratedValues and 3.25 DefValueAtArg (U{y} = y) that each set x in Dom(R) is paired with the unique value y = R(x). In 3.89-3.90, SetRankLaws(R, V) is carried as an explicit antecedent hypothesis on the rank operator R.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsOrdinal
entries.title: Step 0 of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of a universe is an ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((U universe)—→Ord((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step0_universe_inter_on_is_ordinal : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u : ∀(U:Class)((U universe) —→ ((∅ ∈ U) ∧ ((∅ ∈ (U ∩ On)) ∧ ¬((U ∩ On) = ∅))))): if U is a universe, then U is transitive and On is an ordinal, so their binary intersection kappa = U n On is a transitive class of ordinals and hence an ordinal.

entries.name: ThmUniverseUnionClosedFromIndexedUnion
entries.title: Step 1a of U = V_(U n On): a transitive class closed under indexed unions is closed under unary union
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)∀(f:Class)(((Tr(U)∧IndexedUnionClosed(U))∧((f class-function)∧((V⊆Dom(f))∧∀(a:Class)(f(a)=a))))—→∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step1a_union_closed_from_indexed_union : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): instantiating IndexedUnionClosed(U) with I = x in U and an identity class-function witness f on V yields f[x] = x c U and hence U(x) in U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseInterOnIsLimitOrdinal
entries.title: Step 1c of U = V_(U n On): the ordinal trace U n On of an union-closed universe is a nonzero limit ordinal
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))—→LimitOrd((U∩On))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step1c_kappa_is_limit_ord : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): for any universe U closed under unary union, kappa = U n On is an ordinal, contains 0 (via thm_step0_universe_emptyset_in_u from ω ∈ U and Hereditary(U)), and is closed under ordinal successor B |-> B u {B} = U({B, {B}}) by pairing and union closure; therefore LimitOrd(U n On) holds.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannStageSubUniverse
entries.title: Step 2 of U = V_(U n On): limit-stage inclusion V_(U n On) c= U from stage closure below U n On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(Tr(U)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))))—→(V((U∩On))⊆U)))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step2_v_kappa_sub_u : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the base and successor step lemmas thm_step2_v_0_in_u, thm_step2_v_succ_in_u, and thm_step2_v_limit_fam_sub_u): under VStageLaws(V), Trans(U), LimitOrd(U n On), and the stage-closure premise ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, unfolding the limit clause V(U n On) = U_{B ∈ U n On} V(B) and applying transitivity of U yields V(U n On) c= U.

entries.name: ThmUniverseSubVonNeumannStage
entries.title: Step 3 of U = V_(U n On): rank-bounded inclusion U c= V_(U n On) from stage and rank closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(V:Class)∀(R:Class)∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(V)∧(SetRankLaws(R,V)∧(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(V(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(R(x)∈U))))))—→(U⊆V((U∩On)))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_step3_u_sub_v_kappa : Thm, accompanied in universe_definitions.ML by the inductive rank-successor step lemma thm_step3_rank_succ_in_u): under VStageLaws(V), SetRankLaws(R, V), LimitOrd(U n On), stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, every a ∈ U has R(a) ∈ (U n On), R(a) u {R(a)} ∈ (U n On) by limit closure, and a ∈ V(R(a) u {R(a)}) c= V(U n On), concluding U c= V(U n On).

entries.name: ThmUniverseEqVonNeumannStageInterOn
entries.title: Conclusion of U = V_(U n On): combining Step 1c, Step 2, and Step 3 under stage, rank, and union closure
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(U:Class)((VStageLaws(VStageGraph)∧(SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph,VStageGraph)∧(((U universe)∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(⋃x∈U)))∧((∀(B:Class)((B∈(U∩On))—→(VStageGraph(B)∈U)))∧∀(x:Class)((x∈U)—→(SetRankGraph(x)∈U))))))—→(LimitOrd((U∩On))∧(U=VStageGraph((U∩On))))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system synthesis theorem (thm_universe_eq_canonical_v_inter_on and thm_universe_eq_v_inter_on : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check across the 45 constituent lemmas in universe_definitions.ML Section 11): given VStageLaws(VStageGraph), SetRankLaws(SetRankGraph, VStageGraph), Universe(U) with unary union closure, stage closure ∀B ∈ (U n On), V(B) ∈ U, and rank closure ∀x ∈ U, R(x) ∈ U, combines Step 1c (LimitOrd(U n On)), Step 2 (V_(U n On) c= U), and Step 3 (U c= V_(U n On)) via class equality antisymmetry (EqDef) to conclude LimitOrd(U n On) /\ (U = VStageGraph(U n On)).

entries.name: DefDomainRestriction
entries.title: Restriction of a class relation or function to a domain class
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)(Restrict(F,A)={z|(z∈F)∧(pr1(z)∈A)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefDomainRestriction, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): Restrict(F, A) = { z : Class | (z in F) /\ (pr1(z) in A) } restricts a class relation or function F to arguments whose first Dunaev projection belongs to A.

entries.name: DefTransfiniteApproximation
entries.title: Transfinite recursion approximation predicate on ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,g)←→((g function)∧((Dom(g)∈On)∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈Dom(g))∧(X=Restrict(g,B)))—→(g(B)=G(X)))))))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteApproximation, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): TransfiniteApprox(G, g) holds iff g is a set-sized function whose domain Dom(g) belongs to On and for all B in Dom(g) and X = Restrict(g, B), valOf(g, B) = valOf(G, X).

entries.name: DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph
entries.title: Canonical transfinite recursion class-function graph on On
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)(TransfiniteRec(G)=⋃{g|TransfiniteApprox(G,g)}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefTransfiniteRecursionGraph, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g : Class | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) } is the union of the class A(G) of all set-sized transfinite approximations for generator G.

entries.name: DefVonNeumannStepGenerator
entries.title: Von Neumann cumulative hierarchy transfinite step generator
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)(VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈Dom(f))∧(Y=𝒫(f(B))))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefVonNeumannStepGenerator, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): VonNeumannStepG(f) = U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in Dom(f)) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(f, B))) } maps any set-sized ordinal approximation f to the union of the powersets of its values.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteApproxCoherence
entries.title: Step 1 of Transfinite Recursion on On: coherence of approximations on common ordinal domains
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(h:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)∧(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((∀(B:Class)∀(z:Class)(((pr1(z)∈B)∧(g(pr1(z))=h(pr1(z))))—→((z∈g)←→(z∈h))))∧(A∈(Dom(g)∩Dom(h))))))—→((Restrict(g,A)=Restrict(h,A))∧((g(A)=G(Restrict(g,A)))∧(g(A)=h(A))))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_transfinite_approx_coherence and thm_transfinite_approx_coherence_step : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_1 = { B : Class | (B in (Dom(g) n Dom(h))) -> (valOf(g, B) = valOf(h, B)) } using transitivity of the ordinal intersection Dom(g) n Dom(h) (thm_bininter_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below), concluding Restrict(g, A) = Restrict(h, A) and valOf(g, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(g, A)) = valOf(h, A) for all A in Dom(g) n Dom(h).

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionEquation
entries.title: Steps 2 and 3 of Transfinite Recursion on On: approximation sethood, union inclusion, and global recursion equation F(A) = G(Restrict(F, A)) from witnessing approximations
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(g:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(A:Class)((TransfiniteApprox(G,g)—→((g set)∧(g⊆TransfiniteRec(G))))∧(((∀(B:Class)((B∈On)—→∃(h:Class)(TransfiniteApprox(G,h)∧((B∈Dom(h))∧((F(B)=h(B))∧(Restrict(F,B)=Restrict(h,B)))))))∧(A∈On))—→(F(A)=G(Restrict(F,A))))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_transfinite_recursion_equation, thm_approx_is_set, thm_in_approx_class_iff, thm_approx_sub_transfinite_rec, and thm_restrict_agree_from_sub : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proves (1) unconditionally that every G-approximation g is a set and a subclass of TransfiniteRec(G) = U { g | TransfiniteApprox(G, g) }, and (2) that whenever each ordinal B in On has a witnessing approximation h in A(G) with B in Dom(h), F(B) = h(B), and Restrict(F, B) = Restrict(h, B), the global recursion equation valOf(F, A) = valOf(G, Restrict(F, A)) holds for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmTransfiniteRecursionUniqueness
entries.title: Step 4 of Transfinite Recursion on On: uniqueness of the transfinite recursion class-function
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(G:Class)∀(F:Class)∀(H:Class)∀(A:Class)((((∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(F,B)))—→(F(B)=G(X))))∧∀(B:Class)∀(X:Class)(((B∈On)∧(X=Restrict(H,B)))—→(H(B)=G(X))))∧((∀(B:Class)∀(z:Class)(((pr1(z)∈B)∧(F(pr1(z))=H(pr1(z))))—→((z∈F)←→(z∈H))))∧(A∈On)))—→((Restrict(F,A)=Restrict(H,A))∧(F(A)=H(A)))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness and thm_transfinite_recursion_uniqueness_step : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proved by genuine transfinite epsilon-induction (EpsIndAx) on K_4 = { B : Class | (B in On) -> (valOf(F, B) = valOf(H, B)) } using transitivity of On (thm_on_is_transitive) and extensional restriction equality (thm_restrict_eq_from_below), concluding Restrict(F, A) = Restrict(H, A) and valOf(F, A) = valOf(H, A) for all A in On.

entries.name: ThmVonNeumannHierarchyByTransfiniteRecursion
entries.title: Application of Transfinite Recursion on On: base-stage law and unfolding of VonNeumannStepG(f) = U_(B in A) P(V_B)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(f:Class)∀(V:Class)∀(A:Class)(((∀(B:Class)¬(B∈Dom(f)))—→(VonNeumannStepG(f)=∅))∧(((V(A)=VonNeumannStepG(f))∧((Dom(f)=A)∧∀(B:Class)((B∈A)—→(f(B)=V(B)))))—→((VonNeumannStepG(f)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})∧(V(A)=⋃{Y|∃(B:Class)((B∈A)∧(Y=𝒫(V(B))))})))))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_von_neumann_hierarchy_by_recursion, thm_von_neumann_step_g_empty, thm_von_neumann_step_g_on_stage, and thm_power_cong : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proves (1) unconditionally that VonNeumannStepG(f) = ∅ whenever Dom(f) is empty, and (2) by unfolding DefVonNeumannStepGenerator and applying powerclass congruence (thm_power_cong: P = Q -> Pow(P) = Pow(Q)) that whenever Dom(f) = A, f agrees with V on A, and V(A) = VonNeumannStepG(f), both VonNeumannStepG(f) and V(A) equal U { Y : Class | exists (B:Class), (B in A) /\ (Y = Pow(valOf(V, B))) }.

entries.title: Generalisation
entries.prf_constructor: PMetaGen_prf (Γ, x, x', T, PForaR_prf (Γ, x, x', T, p))

entries.name: DefMetaConecessitation
entries.title: CoNecessitation
entries.status: Primitive / Derived Rule (Metalevel for 𝘍, Instance Verified)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(Γ:Ctx)∀(𝛗:Fm)((𝘍,[]⊢‹𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗›)—→(𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗)))
entries.comment: If a formula  is derived in 𝘍 from the empty context, then the formula 𝛗 is derived in 𝘍 from the context Γ. Why this holds for 𝘍: for an arbitrary theory 𝘞, concluding (𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗) from (𝘞, [] ⊢ ) requires 1-consistency / Σ₁-soundness of 𝘞 (and for the r.e. base theory 𝘛, asserting internal co-necessitation would by Löb's theorem 5.01 trivialize 𝘛). Because 𝘍 is a non-r.e. sound Henkin extension equipped with Soundness 3.72 ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) → ⟦ψ⟧), instantiating 3.72 at ψ :=  directly yields (𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗).

entries.name: AxmMetaClassComprehension
entries.title: Class comprehension axiom schema

entries.comment: Postulated +1 metalevel class comprehension schema guarded by Fm.FFI(k, x, φ), accompanied by a kernel-checked object-level instance (thm_4_06_meta_class_comprehension / sequent_4_06_comprehension : Thm, checked by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check).

entries.name: DefReducedVarSubst
entries.title: Reduced object-level variable substitution operator SubstVar(t, x, v)
entries.formula_unicode_html: (∀(t:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(SubstVar(t,x,v)={u|((v=x)∧(u∈t))∨((¬(v=x))∧(u∈v))}))
entries.comment: Conservative definition (DefReducedVarSubst, PKernelDef_prf, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): explicit 3-argument object-level substitution operator SubstVar(t, x, v) = { u : Class | (((v = x) /\ (u in t)) \/ ((~(v = x)) /\ (u in v))) } taking (1) what is being substituted (t), (2) instead of what (x), and (3) where (v), internalizing atomic variable substitution as a first-class object inside MKTD1-theory.

entries.name: ThmReducedVarSubstLaws
entries.title: Hit, miss, idempotence, and diagonal evaluation laws of reduced object-level variable substitution SubstVar(t, x, v)
entries.formula_unicode_html: ((∀(t:Class)∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(((v=x)—→(SubstVar(t,x,v)=t))∧((¬(v=x))—→(SubstVar(t,x,v)=v))))∧((∀(x:Class)∀(v:Class)(SubstVar(x,x,v)=v))∧∀(a:Class)∀(x:Class)(SubstVar(a,x,x)=a)))
entries.comment: Machine-checked MKTD1-system theorem (thm_reduced_var_subst_laws, thm_reduced_var_subst_hit, thm_reduced_var_subst_miss, thm_reduced_var_subst_idempotent_self, and thm_reduced_var_subst_chain_same_var : Thm, verified by Thm.checkPipeline and Thm.slow_check): proves inside MKTD1-theory the hit law (v = x) -> (SubstVar(t, x, v) = t), the miss law (~(v = x)) -> (SubstVar(t, x, v) = v), the self-substitution identity SubstVar(x, x, v) = v, and the diagonal evaluation identity SubstVar(a, x, x) = a.

entries.comment: Verified in IncompletenessMechanization.derive_loeb_trace (incompleteness.ML:1103-1215, 10-step derivation of Löb's theorem from the Diagonal Lemma fixed point ψ ⟷ ((𝘛, [] ⊢ ψ) —→ φ), Hilbert-Bernays-Löb derivability conditions D1-D3, and propositional axioms A01, A02, MP, bridged to a 10-node kernel certificate in IncompletenessMKTD1Kernel). Here 𝘌 ∈ {IΣ₁, PA, 𝘛, NBG, MK} is an unspecified elementary metatheory capable of proving HBL conditions D1-D3 for the r.e. base theory 𝘛 (specifically D3, formalized / internal Σ₁-completeness ψ —→ Pr_𝘛(⌜ψ⌝), which requires Σ₁-induction IΣ₁ and cannot be proved inside Robinson's arithmetic Q even though Q is externally Σ₁-complete for true Σ₁ sentences; see Hájek & Pudlák 1993; Bezboruah & Shepherdson 1976; Boolos 1993).
